name: LEAF (Local Enhancement & Appreciation of Forests)
summary: Plant and care for native trees and shrubs, help look after demonstration gardens, or join community outreach.
scope: Garden teams in Toronto. Planting events in Toronto, York Region and Durham Region.
commitment: No minimum stated. Planting runs spring (Apr to Jun) and fall (Sep to Oct). Garden teams run Apr to Nov.
who: Planting events: any age (under 16 with an adult). More involved roles: 18+ after an orientation.
signup: Interest form, then a volunteer orientation, then the Volunteer Callout email list.
notConfirmed: Current event dates (they send these through their callout list)

name: TRCA: Community Events volunteer
summary: Help Toronto and Region Conservation Authority staff run public events such as guided hikes, tree plantings, litter cleanups and festival booths. Training is provided.
commitment: Variable hours. This posting runs March 1 to December 31, 2026.
notConfirmed: Which specific locations. Events vary, so distance here is only to Toronto.

name: Evergreen
summary: Volunteer with public markets, gardening and stewardship (composting, invasive plant removal), festivals and events, or children and youth programs.
scope: Festivals and events are mainly at Evergreen Brick Works. Children and youth programs are in Toronto.
commitment: Not stated. Gardening sessions run days and evenings. Most youth roles need onboarding and training.
who: Minimum age not stated. Gardening welcomes all experience levels.
signup: Register to volunteer through Better Impact.

name: Toronto Wildlife Centre
summary: Help with wildlife care, education, grocery runs and other operations. Skilled volunteers (accounting, event planning, carpentry) are welcome. Internships and student placements are available.
scope: Their volunteer page doesn't say where roles take place.
who: Not stated. Check their Volunteer FAQ.
notConfirmed: Whether they are accepting new volunteers right now

name: City of Toronto: park, tree and environment volunteering
summary: Community stewardship in parks, trail care events, tree planting, Tree Planting Captain, and climate and waste-reduction ambassador programs.
commitment: Varies by program. Some are short-term events.
signup: Pick a program from their list. Each program has its own page.

name: Credit Valley Conservation
summary: Lead community stewardship events (tree plantings, invasive species removal, litter cleanups), help at Maple Syrup in the Park, or join the youth stewardship program.
scope: Mississauga, Brampton, Orangeville, Erin, Halton Hills and Caledon.
commitment: Stewardship leaders: at least four events a year. Youth leaders: at least once a week, Monday to Friday.
who: Youth Stewardship Volunteer Leader: ages 18 to 29.
signup: Online application during the recruitment period.
season: Their page says applications open in February and March, so this may be closed right now.
notConfirmed: Whether applications are open right now

name: Ocean Wise Shoreline Cleanup
summary: Join or lead a cleanup of a shoreline near you. Individuals, families and community groups can take part.
scope: Anywhere you can find or lead a shoreline cleanup.
signup: Use the Join or Lead a Shoreline Cleanup page on their site.
confirmed: Program exists and is run by Ocean Wise
notConfirmed: Specific Toronto or GTA cleanups (their page lists none)

name: Volunteer Toronto
summary: A volunteer centre that matches people with Toronto organizations that need help. Use it to look beyond this list.
signup: Browse their opportunities and apply to the organization you pick.
notConfirmed: How to search by area or cause (check their site)
